newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran blasts German verdict as biased, unfounded.
newsitem.headline: Iran blasts German verdict as biased, unfounded.

text.p: Iran on Thursday rejected as biased the ruling by a German court that Tehran ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents, and said Tehran had withdrawn its ambassador to Germany for consultations.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi said the rulings by the German court were unfounded and influenced by a propaganda campaign launched against Iran, the official IRNA news agency reported.

"The reality is that the statements of the Berlin court judge have been made in an unjust and biased manner based on the false claims of counter revolutionary elements and hostile political propaganda of the Zionists, and thus are rejected and condemned by us," Mohammadi said.

"We are awaiting a detailed and official account of the court procedures in order to scrutinise the issue," he said, adding that Iran had recalled its ambassador to Bonn, Hossein Moussavian, for consultations.

In its Thursday ruling, the court avoided citing names but gave the positions of the Iranian officials it believed were behind the murders as members of a committee which included the state president and Iran's religious leader.

Iran's ties with Germany, Tehran's main trade partner, were strained by German charges that spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani ordered the murders. Iran has denied being involved.
